heroLead: West Alexander sits right on the West Virginia line in western Washington County, in some of the richest wet gas ground the Marcellus has to offer.
intro: We grew up two counties over from West Alexander, and the story there is the same one our own family lived through: a grandfather's farm that got leased in the boom years, then split a dozen ways by the time the grandkids inherited it. If your name is on a deed near West Alexander because of a will, not a purchase, you are the exact person we built this business for.

This corner of Washington County sits over the wet gas fairway of the Marcellus, where the shale runs rich in ethane and propane alongside the methane. That mix is part of why operators pushed hard into this ground starting in the late 2000s, and why so many older leases here still carry outdated royalty language.

sections.heading: Why West Alexander Ground Draws Interest
paragraphs: West Alexander's position near the state line puts it inside the wet gas fairway that made Washington County one of the busiest counties in the play. Liquids-rich production means the gas itself is worth more at the wellhead, which is exactly why leasing activity here ran hot compared to the drier gas counties to the north.

That does not mean every parcel is treated the same by every buyer. Spacing units, unit participation, and whether your tract sits in a producing pool or just an offset area all change what an interest is worth. We look at your actual lease and your actual royalty statements before we say anything about value.

sections.heading: The Deduction Problem We Keep Seeing
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act says a lease can't pay less than one-eighth net, but 'net' is where families near West Alexander keep getting hurt. Post-production costs, gathering fees, compression, marketing charges, get deducted before the check is cut. We've read enough of these statements from our own family's parcel to know how far a royalty can shrink once those lines start stacking up.

If your monthly check has been sliding for reasons the operator never really explains, that is often the deduction language working exactly as the lease was written, not a mistake. It is one of the biggest reasons owners near this fairway decide selling now beats waiting on statements they cannot fully audit.

sections.heading: Clean Title Starts at the Washington County Courthouse
paragraphs: Every deal we do near West Alexander runs through the recorder of deeds in Washington. Old severed mineral estates, heir property that never got probated cleanly, and decades-old leases with vague habendum clauses are common out here, and they slow a closing down if nobody catches them early.
We do that title work ourselves before we ever put a number in front of you, so you are not the one chasing down a 1970s deed reference at the courthouse to figure out what you actually own.

faqs.question: Is West Alexander really in the core Marcellus play?
faqs.answer: It's on the western edge of Washington County's wet gas fairway, which is generally considered strong ground, though value still depends on your specific tract, unit, and lease terms rather than the county name alone.

faqs.question: I inherited a fraction of an interest near West Alexander. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fractional and heir interests are common in this area and are exactly the kind of deal we specialize in. We'll walk you through what documentation the courthouse will need.

faqs.question: Do you charge anything to look at my lease and statements?
faqs.answer: No. We review your documents and give you a straight answer about whether we're interested, at no cost to you.

faqs.question: What if my lease is old and I don't have a copy?
faqs.answer: We can usually pull it from the Washington County recorder of deeds ourselves as part of our title review, so a missing copy isn't a dead end.
